title: Small farms face H-2A application and compliance paperwork; burden estimates are disputed

history.reason: Signal from DOL final rule and public comments.

description: Agricultural employers using the H-2A program file job orders and certification applications with addenda; DOL estimates small burden while industry commenters call the estimate a gross underestimation.
customer_segment: H-2A employers, most of them small (DOL found 82.5 percent of the matched sample small, average 11 employees).
context: Based on the April 2024 final rule; the rule's later status and DOL processing changes were not checked.

evidence.text: DOL found 2,159 of 2,615 matched H-2A employers (82.5 percent) were small, averaging 11 employees and about $3.6 million revenue.
An industry commenter asserted DOL's burden estimate was drastically low.
H-2A employers may spend material staff time or consultant fees on applications and records.

alternatives: Agricultural labor contractors, associations and attorneys who file on behalf of farms: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: DOL's own analysis estimates a low per-employer burden; the dispute is between agency and commenters and is not resolved by this source.

uncertainty: Unknown: actual time and fees per application, how many farms use agents, and who buys software.
open_questions: What do H-2A employers or their agents actually spend per season?
Do agents already automate this work?
next_actions: Find independent data on H-2A filing cost and agent usage.
